newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds pare gains on U.S. data, profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds pare gains on U.S. data, profit-taking.

text.p: Irish government bonds retreated in afternoon trade on Monday after charging forward at the open, as profit-taking and stronger-than-expected U.S. data eroded early gains, dealers said.
But they said bonds had still outperformed Bunds and gilts over the day and the underlying tone was healthy.
"The numbers in the U.S. have pulled down markets everywhere," one dealer said.

"Also, the gains in the Irish market were maybe a bit overdone this morning," he said. "We were sharply ahead this morning, with good foreign buying and maybe a bit of a short squeeze, and we've had a slight correction this afternoon."
By 1605 GMT the 6.5 percent bond due 2006 was 50p higher at 101.65 to yield 6.09 percent, while the eight percent bond due 2006 was up 70p at 108.85, yielding 6.72 percent.
Dealers said the market's strong early gains were fuelled by convergence trades after Friday's European Union agreement on a stability pact for the single currency.

U.S. November industrial output was up 0.9 percent, the largest increase since February and well above the forecast 0.6 percent rise. "The U.S. numbers have dampened things down but it has still been a good day for Irish bonds," a dealer said.
